audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly validate Bloom filter size invariant to prevent consensus divergence?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the EL node's Bloom filter validation. Prysm is a CL client. The CL receives LogsBloom via EngineAPI as a fixed-size SSZ field (ssz-size:256 in proto/engine/v1/execution_engine.pb.go:93). Prysm does not independently validate the 256-byte Bloom filter invariant - it relies on SSZ fixed-size enforcement and trusts the EL's validation. No extract-and-validate path for Bloom filter size exists in Prysm's CL code.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is the EIP-7702 Authorization tuple strictly validated to contain exactly the required 6 fields?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EIP-7702 Authorization tuples and RLP decoding are pure EL concepts. Prysm (CL client) does not implement EIP-7702 transaction processing, Authorization tuple parsing, or RLP decoding. No references to EIP-7702 or Authorization tuple validation exist in the Prysm codebase. The 'Authorization' references in Prysm are HTTP authorization headers (network/endpoint.go), not EIP-7702.

audit_items.title: Does the EL Node correctly reject Authorization tuples with incorrect field count during RLP parsing?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: RLP parsing of EIP-7702 Authorization tuples is an EL-only operation. Prysm is a CL client that uses SSZ encoding, not RLP. No RLP parsing code exists in Prysm for Authorization tuple handling. The EL node actor referenced is not implemented in this codebase.

audit_items.title: Is the EIP-7702 Authorizer protected against signature verification failures caused by malformed Authorization field types?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: EIP-7702 Authorizer signature verification is an EL-only operation. Prysm (CL client) does not implement the EIP-7702 authorizer role. The actor-eip7702-authorizer referenced in this check does not exist in Prysm. No secp256k1 signature recovery for EIP-7702 Authorization tuples is implemented in this codebase.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is ALL data received from P2P peers fully validated before processing?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets EL node P2P validation (tb-005 is an EL trust boundary). The specific validation items mentioned (account RLP encoding, deposit data format, Authorization signature format, requests hash computation inputs) are all EL-specific operations. Prysm's P2P layer handles CL-specific messages (beacon blocks, attestations, etc.) using SSZ encoding, not the EL P2P protocol with RLP encoding.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node have comprehensive validation for all P2P-received data types before state transitions?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check explicitly targets the EL node (actor-el-node) and its P2P data validation before state transitions. Prysm is a CL client. EL state transitions (account balance updates, contract execution, transaction processing) are not implemented in Prysm. The EL P2P protocol and message types referenced here are separate from Prysm's CL P2P layer.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is RLP-encoded account data from P2P peers validated against size constraints before parsing?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: RLP-encoded account data is an EL-specific concept. Prysm (CL client) uses SSZ encoding for all its data structures, not RLP. The P2P message handlers in Prysm deal with beacon blocks, attestations, and other CL messages - not RLP-encoded account data. Trust boundary tb-005 references the EL P2P boundary.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly reject malformed RLP data from untrusted P2P peers without excessive resource consumption?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check explicitly targets the EL node's RLP data handling from P2P peers. Prysm is a CL client that does not process RLP-encoded data from P2P peers. No RLP decoder implementation exists in Prysm's production code.

audit_items.title: Are there pre-allocation limits enforced in the RLP decoder to prevent memory exhaustion attacks?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: RLP decoder pre-allocation limits are an EL-specific concern. Prysm (CL) uses SSZ encoding with fixed-size fields defined in protobuf schemas (e.g., ssz-size annotations). The actor-p2p-peer referenced here refers to an EL P2P peer, not the CL P2P peer implemented by Prysm.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is per-deposit-event CPU cost in extract_deposit_data bounded to prevent DoS?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: extract_deposit_data is an EL-specific function that parses deposit contract event log data. This function does not exist in Prysm's CL codebase. Prysm receives deposit requests already parsed by the EL via EngineAPI as ExecutionRequests (proto/engine/v1/electra.go). The CPU cost of extract_deposit_data is an EL concern.

audit_items.title: Does the P2P peer enforce rate limiting or early rejection of blocks with excessive deposit events?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the EL P2P peer (actor-p2p-peer) and its handling of blocks with excessive deposit events. In Prysm's CL, deposit events are received as already-processed DepositRequest objects via ExecutionRequests from the EngineAPI, not as raw deposit events in P2P blocks. The EL P2P rate limiting referenced here is outside the CL client's scope.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node maintain acceptable block processing throughput at maximum deposit event capacity?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets EL node (actor-el-node) block processing throughput for deposit events. Block processing of deposit events (extract_deposit_data) is an EL-specific operation. Prysm (CL) receives deposit data already extracted by the EL. The throughput concern for deposit event processing applies to the EL implementation, not the CL.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002/tb-003: Is malformed deposit event data from DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS properly detected and does it cause block rejection?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets EL-side deposit event validation from the DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS. Trust boundaries tb-002 (deposit contract to EL) and tb-003 (EL to CL) are EL-side boundaries. The extract_deposit_data function and deposit event parsing referenced here are EL operations. While Prysm does process DepositRequest objects received from the EL (proto/engine/v1/electra.go), it does not parse raw deposit event data from the deposit contract directly.

audit_items.title: Does the deposit contract interaction path enforce strict data format requirements before emitting events?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the deposit contract (actor-deposit-contract) and its event emission logic. The deposit contract is an on-chain Solidity smart contract executed by the EVM on the EL. Prysm (CL) does not implement or interact with the deposit contract's event emission logic. The CL receives deposit data already processed by the EL.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly validate and sanitize deposit event data before forwarding to consensus layer?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the EL node (actor-el-node) and its responsibility for validating deposit event data before forwarding to the CL. This is an EL-side validation step. The CL side (Prysm) receives the data via EngineAPI and processes it via GetDecodedExecutionRequests (proto/engine/v1/electra.go), but the validation and sanitization before forwarding is the EL's responsibility.

audit_items.title: Does the block producer correctly reject blocks with malformed deposit data rather than propagating invalid blocks?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the block producer (actor-block-producer) at the EL level and its handling of malformed deposit data. While Prysm does propose beacon blocks, the deposit data malformation check referenced here is about the EL-side block production (constructing execution payloads with deposit data). The CL block proposal in Prysm receives execution payloads from the EL via EngineAPI and trusts them after basic structural validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Is Uint.from_be_bytes offset parsing protected against integer overflow in fixed-width implementations?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: Uint.from_be_bytes offset parsing in extract_deposit_data is an EL-specific operation. This function parses raw deposit contract event log data using big-endian byte parsing. Prysm (CL) does not implement extract_deposit_data or parse raw deposit event bytes. The CL receives already-structured DepositRequest protobuf objects via the EngineAPI. Trust boundary tb-002 (deposit contract to EL) is entirely on the EL side.

audit_items.title: Are bounds checks enforced on parsed offset values before they are used for data extraction?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the deposit contract (actor-deposit-contract) and offset bounds checking in deposit data extraction. Prysm (CL) does not parse deposit data offsets. The deposit data extraction from raw event logs, including offset parsing and bounds checking, is entirely an EL-side operation.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node properly validate deposit data offsets before extracting and processing deposit information?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the EL node (actor-el-node) and its deposit data offset validation. Prysm is a CL client and does not implement deposit data offset parsing. The test procedure references Go, Rust, and Java EL client implementations - Prysm is a Go CL client, not an EL client. The checked_add/checked_sub and safe integer parsing mentioned are EL implementation details.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Is compute_requests_hash deterministic across all execution paths and thread contexts?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: compute_requests_hash is an EL function. In Prysm's codebase, CalcRequestsHash appears only in testing middleware (testing/middleware/builder/builder.go:963) where it calls gethTypes.CalcRequestsHash - this delegates to the go-ethereum library for testing purposes only. Trust boundary tb-004 (EL internal API/EngineAPI) is an EL-side boundary. The production CL code does not compute requests hashes; it receives them from the EL via EngineAPI.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node produce identical requests hash outputs for identical block data across restarts and different instances?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the EL node (actor-el-node) and its requests hash computation consistency. Prysm (CL) does not produce requests hashes in production code - it receives them from the EL via EngineAPI. The determinism of compute_requests_hash is an EL implementation concern.

audit_items.title: Does the CL node validate and agree on requests hash values consistently with the EL?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: While this check references the CL node (actor-cl-node), it focuses on how the CL validates requests hash from the EL. In Prysm's architecture, the requests hash validation is delegated to the EL via the EngineAPI newPayload call. The CL does not independently recompute the requests hash - it trusts the EL's validation result. The CalcRequestsHash in Prysm only exists in testing code (testing/middleware/builder/builder.go), not in production CL validation paths. ProcessPayload in beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go validates only parent_hash, prevRandao, and timestamp - not requests hash.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Are buffer read bounds in extract_deposit_data properly validated against attacker-controlled deposit data?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: extract_deposit_data and its buffer read operations are EL-specific functions. Prysm (CL) does not implement extract_deposit_data. Trust boundary tb-002 (deposit contract to EL node) is entirely on the EL side. The CL receives DepositRequest objects already deserialized by the EL, with size validation handled via SSZ fixed-size constraints in proto/engine/v1/electra.go.

audit_items.title: Does the deposit contract interface provide length validation before data is passed to extract_deposit_data?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: The deposit contract interface and extract_deposit_data function are EL-specific components. The actor-deposit-contract referenced here is an on-chain smart contract interacted with by the EL, not the CL. Prysm (CL) does not directly interact with the deposit contract or implement extract_deposit_data.

audit_items.title: Does the EL node maintain memory safety invariants when processing untrusted deposit data from external sources?
audit_items.scope_reason: Component mismatch: This check targets the EL node (actor-el-node) and its memory safety when processing raw deposit data. Prysm (CL) does not process raw deposit data from external sources. The CL receives structured DepositRequest protobuf objects from the EL via EngineAPI. Prysm's handling of deposit data (proto/engine/v1/electra.go unmarshalDeposits) uses SSZ with fixed-size items and enforced limits (maxDepositRequests), which is a different concern from the EL's raw buffer processing.
